Shuffle diagnostics measure a fitted model’s sensitivity to a specified perturbation distribution; they do not establish causal effects or higher-order sequence understanding. Sequential-recommendation research shows that shuffle design matters: arbitrary versus availability-constrained shuffles can disrupt different signals. General permutation-importance research also warns that breaking dependencies can create unrealistic inputs and misleading interpretations. [Sequential-data study](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/), [permutation interpretation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.03151).

Mathematically, uniform full-history shuffling randomizes both the endpoint and earlier positions; final-item-fixed prefix shuffling randomizes earlier positions conditional on preserving the endpoint. Their sensitivity difference therefore contrasts two intervention distributions, rather than isolating “last-item importance.” Full shuffling also changes which items occupy the prefix and how they connect to the endpoint. With n nonpadding interactions and m occurrences of the original final item, full shuffling preserves its final identity with probability m/n—not necessarily 1/n. Duplicate-item swaps can leave inputs unchanged. Report actual changed-position counts, endpoint-change rates, sequence lengths, and unchanged-input rates; shuffle only nonpadding positions.

A proposed tighter control: compare one transposition involving the final position with one wholly within the prefix, matched on swap distance, unequal item identities, sequence length, and available item-frequency characteristics. Use the same users, candidates, and repeated paired draws; report uncertainty and both ranking changes and validation HR@10 changes. This better matches perturbation magnitude, although neighboring transitions and positional context still differ. Interpret the contrast as endpoint-involving versus prefix-only swap sensitivity. Small prefix-shuffle effects do not prove earlier history is unused: its item identities may contribute through order-insensitive aggregation.
